text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government will introduce foreclosure laws to recover loans through liquidation of assets without following a long litigation process, says Commerce Minister Ishaq Dar.

- U.S. Ambassador to Pakistan, Thomas Simons Jr, has suggested setting up export processing zones as the only solution for Pakistan to overcome problems like workers' rights which hamper its foreign trade.

- The Pakistan Air Force has recommended to the Defence Ministry that Squadron Leader Muhammad Farooq, who was arrested in the United States for allegedly smuggling two kg of heroin, should be brought back to Pakistan for further interrogation.
- Pakistan needs to mobilise an additional $1 billion in the current calendar year to import about four million tonnes of wheat to bridge the supply-demand gap in the next 12 months.
- The government may consider imposing a federal tax on agricultural income in the 1997/98 (July-June) budget to broaden the tax base, chairman of the private Human Resource Centre Mahbubul Haq said.

- Pakistan has welcomed the appointment of Inder Kumar Gujral as the new Indian Prime Minister and hoped all pending problems between the two countries, including the core issue of Kashmir, would be settled.
- The Karachi Stock Exchange has decided to dispose of a membership in order to settle outstanding claims against the deals of fake shares of FFC Jordan Fertiliser and Hub Power Co.

- The government is expected to make separate allocations in next year's budget for hydro-electric power projects to be executed under the Private Sector Energy Development Fund after announcement of a new policy for private sector hydel projects.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan will provide resources to commercial banks under the export re-finance scheme at 10 percent mark-up rate.
- Pakistan will seek $2.26 billion from the Aid-to-Pakistan Consortium meeting in Paris.
- Police have arrested a man allegedly involved in killing seven people at the Iranian consulate in Multan in March.
